units.account: Col. Aubry has no new order and holds his line south of the river, facing the bridge. He sees the cavalry go out and come back, and nothing threatens him.
Col. Delacroix has no new order and holds his line beside the 1st Battalion. He sees nothing to commit his reserve to.

Maj. Verneuil gets his order in the second minute and goes at once after the fugitives, who are strung out on the road about 250 m ahead. He rides them down in a couple of minutes, sabring many and taking a good number of prisoners, and drives the rest on. At the level of the southern edge of the northern wood, which is the limit he was given, he sees a fresh battalion forming line across the road ahead, at about 150 m. Obeying his order, he breaks off, takes a volley from the battalion as he turns, and rides back to the north bank of the river, where he re-forms.
units.departure: Projection holds the cavalry in a long duel with a formed battalion at 70 m, at the end of which it breaks and flees to (2050,1850) with 147 men. Verneuil's order is to come back if he meets formed infantry, and he does, so he breaks off after a single volley at 150 m rather than standing, ending at (2050,1330), active and with 183 men.

units.account: Col. Brandt has no new order, and his broken men are running up the road. The horse is on them within two minutes, and about a hundred are cut down or taken before they reach the line of the second battalion drawn across the road. They pass through its intervals and he rallies the survivors behind it, with the enemy horse turned back. He re-forms what is left in column and stays behind the line.
units.departure: Projection keeps the Vanguard at 380 men, rallied by minute 6 and at (1957,300), as if untouched by the pursuit. With the enemy horse ordered to pursue it and riding it down on the open road, about 110 men are lost, and it ends at (2050,550) with 270 men, well over the 5% tolerance.

units.account: Col. Hartmann gets the order at about the third minute and forms his battalion in line across the road, as ordered, facing south. He opens his intervals to the Vanguard's fugitives and lets them pass through, then closes up and fires one volley at the enemy horse at about 150 m as it breaks off. It has been stopped, so he does not pursue.
Maj. von Reiter has no order and holds his position at the edge of the northern wood, watching.
units.departure: Projection sends the hussars to (2050,1766), in the Blue rear, though there is no order to do so. With no order they stay where they are, so the position differs by well over 100 m.

summary: Blue-3 received its order in the second minute and rode down the broken Vanguard Battalion on the open road. About 110 of its men were cut down or taken. Verneuil stopped at the level of the southern edge of the northern wood, as ordered, on seeing Red-2 forming line across the road. The Vanguard's survivors passed through Red-2's intervals and rallied behind it, with about 270 men and morale 35. Red-2 gave the cavalry a single volley at about 150 m as it broke off, and Blue-3 rode back to the north bank of the river, with about 17 men lost. The projection had Blue-3 stand and fight the battalion and break; the umpire has it obey its order to come back. Red-3 held; the projection moves it without orders. Blue-1 and Blue-2 held and were not engaged.
